Claim: PM loop round 9 · 2026-10-16T09:20Z · the spec half of #23829, the #23808 family. Each Setup help text this card names becomes one plain sentence in an admin's words, and its ADR vocabulary moves to the docblock or comment beside it: the `isDefault`, `managedBy`, `packageId` and `adminScope` help texts in `permission.form.ts`, the `delegatable` help text in `position.form.ts` and the view-form `description` (ADR-0047) in `view.form.ts`. The generated metadata-forms translations regenerate. One PR, `Fixes #23853`.

- Pins that assert the old strings, changed to the new ones and never deleted, including the `bare-type-display-echo-decisions.test.ts`-style ledgers if they carry these leaves.
- One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`.
- ⛔ Not #23829's `domain:services` object descriptions, not any `.describe()` that is not one of these help strings, and no accept set.
Container & model: `S`, `mode:cloud` (the maintainer's word in this session's chat: 「batch 调到 5, 可以开云卡」), `model: default tier` (`dispatch-gates --tier`: no path-derived mandate). String values in form definitions with no accept-set move. Like #23808, a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review is owed only if the diff reaches `packages/spec/src/**` beyond these strings.
Clause-②: no
Responsibility: n/a — Setup copy that teaches ADR vocabulary to an admin (filing gate ④, the spec half of #23829, p2)
Thread-read: none
Ruling-ref: none (#23802's constraint, as #23808 carried it: keep ADR references out of user-facing strings)
Serial constraints cleared:
- The file lists of all open PRs and the latest `Claim:` of every open `pm:dispatched` card were read in this act. No open PR touches the three `*.form.ts` files.
- PR #23846 (#23809, another seat) regenerates the same `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` files from a different source. Whichever lands second merges `main` and regenerates.
- #23829 (`domain:services`, unclaimed) also regenerates them when it lands.
- The byte-identical duplicate #23856 is closed `duplicate` in this act, pointing here.
